artworks.title: Apollo and the Nymph (Roman fresco, House of Apollo, Pompeii)
artworks.description: Roman wall-painting from Pompeii evokes the god's pursuit of woodland nymphs — the same divine pattern Pausanias records at Thebes, where Apollo held the ash-tree nymph Melia and slew her brother Caanthus for burning his precinct. No ancient image names Melia of Thebes by inscription; the Ismenian story survives in the Periegete's account of fountain, tomb, and river.
